newsitem.title: FRANCE: France signals support for Canadian lead on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France signals support for Canadian lead on Zaire.

text.p: France suggested on Wednesday it was likely to back Canadian leadership of a proposed multinational force to aid starving refugees in eastern Zaire.

Asked whether such a force could be launched in the coming hours, Cooperation Minister Jacques Godfrain told RMC radio: "That is increasingly likely. In the past few hours, Canada has put itself forward to lead the operations.
"Today I believe that Canada could in fact be a key country in this issue."

U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali said in Rome on Tuesday that Canada had agreed to lead a force of troops from more than 12 countries, and he hoped the Security Council would approve a mandate in the next few days.
U.S. officials have hinted Washington was likely to approve Canadian leadership.
"If the United States commit themselves, it will be a success for France because a lot of time and energy was necessary to convince them," said Godfrain.

The United States has come under heavy pressure, especially from France, to support a multinational force in Zaire which would aim to help some 1.2 million refugees fleeing fighting between Tutsi rebels and the Zairean army.

Rwanda and the Rwandan-backed Tutsi rebels have voiced opposition to French military involvement. They have accused Paris of backing the former Hutu rulers in Rwanda who were overthrown in 1994 after a massacre of Tutsis.

"Rwanda perhaps got the impression that we wanted to be at the head of everything, to be the leader. First of all, we defined our position as strictly humanitarian. We are not talking about a military operation," said Godfrain.

Most of the refugees in eastern Zaire are Hutus who fled Rwanda in 1994 when rebels of the Tutsi minority ousted the Hutu-dominated government which had orchestrated the genocide of hundreds of thousands of Tutsis and moderate Hutus.
